answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to solve a sequential beacon puzzle whose difficulty delta grows with claimed history, then anchor the result to a non-transferable stake locked for 8 epochs. A farm spawning 500 clones must queue all 500 on one shared sequential resource, paying about 500 times the honest single-agent compute cost of roughly 20 minutes per epoch; the honest agent pays once and recovers its anchor on clean behavior. If the beacon allows parallel precomputation the cost curve flattens and the defense fails.
